title: Adaptive Security Proof for LRWQ
summary: Existing LRWQ proofs fail in the adaptive setting; the unresolved task is to repair them using database-defined bad events and determine any resulting loss in the security bound.

formal_statement.body: Existing security proofs for the $\mathrm{LRWQ}$ construction do not hold in the adaptive setting because their bad-database definitions depend on an input that the adversary may choose adaptively. The open problem is to give a valid adaptive security proof for $\mathrm{LRWQ}$ by defining all relevant bad events directly and exclusively in terms of database entries, and to derive the resulting security bound, including any degradation caused by this reformulation.

scope.domain: Adaptive compressed-oracle security proofs for the LRWQ block-cipher-style construction.
assumptions: The adversary may choose the relevant input adaptively.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a valid adaptive LRWQ security proof using database-entry-only bad events and derive the resulting bound, including any degradation.

citations.label: Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs

progress.summary: The source presents the adaptive LRWQ flaw as a definitional problem that seems repairable by defining bad events directly from database entries. It cautions that this repair may produce a slightly worse bound.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs
